learner_operation: Identify the specified unchanged pivot row, infer the cleared column from A and B, calculate each of two signed cancellation coefficients, and recognize the operation pair that transforms all entries correctly.

fixed_features.feature: Two row additions on a 3x3 integer matrix using one unchanged pivot row
fixed_features.justification: The KP canonical example 399b7598-c793-5032-9f33-ac02c7b85fe1 and Introduction tutorial teach two successive cancellations; 4x4 and column operations are separate KPs.

fixed_features.feature: Five choices, exactly one correct operation pair
fixed_features.justification: All ten assessed source questions have this radio response contract; the task does not ask which subset of operations is valid.

fixed_features.feature: Small nonzero integer coefficients and nonzero pivot
fixed_features.justification: Preserves easy cancellation arithmetic and two actual row changes. Source example 200a95d9-6cef-55b2-a6a6-5c194d5765aa includes pivot -3; the pivot need not be +1.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Each may occupy any of three positions; no row label is intrinsically correct.
answer_roles.observed: All nine coordinates tested; fixed-A targets (0,0),(0,1),(1,1) produce appropriate changed prompts/solutions.

answer_roles.role: Signs and magnitudes of both coefficients
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Both signs may change independently with corresponding target entries; equal coefficients are legitimate.
answer_roles.observed: Controlled quartets show all four signs for each profile; equal/opposite magnitudes tested in unit banks. Batch alone fixes the first sign relative to its outlier.

answer_roles.role: Extra distractor signs and which coefficient has unit magnitude
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Independent of correct coefficient signs, with distinct mathematically wrong choices.
answer_roles.observed: Revised code separates these assignments. Author test independently rerun: 52 fixed-bank groups; fresh independent quartets confirm the repaired relationship. Current batch accidentally preserves the opposite-sign relation on every item.

coverage.case: Original ten complete banks and canonical example
coverage.result: All complete source banks match; canonical A/B/operations match; canonical answer bank is absent in source.

counterfactuals.expected: First operation changes from -2R1 to +2R1; A, B, intermediate solution and grader key change consistently.
counterfactuals.observed: Same ordered bank, distinct correct choice; exact full-row check, actual screenshots 003/004 and native grading of all choices pass.
counterfactuals.justification: The Introduction tutorial explicitly derives the row multiple needed to cancel the target entry; its sign is not a fixed source-object assignment.

counterfactuals.change: Hold A fixed and change cleared column (0,0)->(0,1), then pivot (0,1)->(1,1).
counterfactuals.expected: B, operation pairs, pivot wording and solution references follow the changed target.
counterfactuals.observed: All-row arithmetic and native grading pass; screenshots of base target and both changes inspected.
counterfactuals.justification: Sources use all pivot-row roles and multiple columns; B and the stated pivot identify the target.

counterfactuals.change: Change base A[1][1] from 5 to 6 while retaining column 0 and both target entries.
counterfactuals.expected: Cancellation coefficients and response preserved; corresponding B and intermediate non-target entry increase by 1.
counterfactuals.observed: Same bank and same correct operation pair; matrices recomputed exactly and actual UI screenshot 005 and native grading agree.
counterfactuals.justification: For a_ic+k*a_pc=0, off-column entries do not affect k; they still must undergo the row operation.

shortcut_probes.cue: First sign of the unique magnitude-pattern outlier among four common-magnitude sign pairs
shortcut_probes.strategy: Take the opposite outlier first sign with the dominant first magnitude; compute only the second row coefficient and select that pair.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Every batch member permits bypassing the first cancellation calculation. This is a finite batch failure, not proof of a universal construction rule.
